messages:
Sam Chen: hey all — first week q: I got a hosted API key but it looks like my requests are getting 429s after a few minutes. I'm mixing embeddings + chat calls in the same process. Is that expected? Any quick tips on how hosted quotas and 'priority buckets' work, and who to ping for a small dev bump?
DevEx Bot: Hi Sam! Quick checks: hosted keys have per-minute token limits and per-minute request limits, plus separate embedding unit budgets. If you hit 429s please include request-id and timestamps when you open a /help ticket. Docs: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/quotas. For short experiments, use your sandbox key to avoid impacting org quotas. :wave:
Priya Patel: welcome Sam — short answer: yes, mixing workloads can surface multiple limits. Embeddings consume embedding units (measured per vector), gen/chat consumes token-rate & concurrency. We also have lightweight "priority buckets" that bias capacity for low-latency interactive traffic vs bulk batch jobs.
Priya Patel: Practical tips: 1) Send embeddings in batched calls (batch_size up to 512 depending on model) to use embedding-specific buckets. 2) Use sandbox for heavy offline runs. 3) If streaming, note that long-lived streams count toward concurrency SLOs.
Matt R.: Also watch concurrent connections; streaming keeps connections open and can spike your concurrency, leading to 429s even if token usage looks fine. For local evals, add a small jitter (100-300ms) between parallel requests or use smaller batch sizes.
Sam Chen: Helpful — thanks. If I open the quota form, who do I cc to speed up a dev bump?
Priya Patel: cc @matt and @ops-team on the quota request. Use the internal quota form: https://redwood.internal/forms/quota-request — include: team, projected rps/tokens, model, whether streaming or long-lived connections, and target timeframe. Small dev bumps usually 24-48h.
Sam Chen: Quick follow: does the hosted key share quota across regions? I'm running tests from eu-west.
Priya Patel: Hosted quota is org-scoped (global) but edge rate-limiting can be region-specific for latency reasons. Dedicated plans can reserve region-specific capacity. If you need region isolation for compliance or predictable latency, file the quota request and mention Dedicated interest.
Sam Chen: Got it. I'll switch heavy runs to sandbox and file the form with metrics. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
DevEx Bot: Helpful checklist: 1) try sandbox for bulk/experiment runs; 2) batch embeddings; 3) reduce streaming concurrency; 4) open quota form + cc ops-team/matt. Ticket template link: https://redwood.internal/help/ticket-template. :white_check_mark:
